Hi Helen — great to hear you and Rajesh are moving this forward.

High level answers up front:
- Readiness checklist: yes — attaching the Redwood Private landing checklist (redwood-private-landing-checklist.pdf). It includes network ports, MTU, NTP/DNS expectations, and recommended VLAN segmentation for tenant isolation.
- KMS/HSM: Redwood Private supports an external KMS via industry-standard KMIP and can integrate with customer HSMs for disk and blob key wrapping. The main constraints are: latency to KMS needs to be under ~100ms for bootstrap tasks; if you want node-boot-time unsealing, ensure the control-plane has a reliable route to the KMS. We also support customer-managed KMS in VPC-only setups.

Quick minimal node mix for a pilot (example):
- 2 control-plane nodes (lightweight, 8 vCPU, 32GB RAM)
- 4 inference worker nodes: 1 x GPU node (A100/80GB or equivalent) + 3 x accelerator-less worker nodes for sidecars and batching orchestration (16 vCPU / 64GB RAM)
- 1 jumpbox + Bastion for admin access

Storage: 1) /var/lib/kubelet on fast NVMe (local SSD) for runtime pods; 2) an NFS or iSCSI block for persistent model artifacts if you prefer shared model store (we recommend object-store-backed model store on-prem if you have S3-compatible storage).

Can you confirm:
- expected latency to the HSM (ms) from the control-plane subnet, and
- whether you have an S3-compatible object store accessible from nodes for model artifacts?

Next steps: I’ll loop in Aisha with an indicative commercial for the pilot and Marissa for deployment runbook assumptions. Do you have a timeline target for the pilot start?

Best,
Aditya Rao
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Hi Helen — looping in a short commercial/ops note so you have options while the technical checks get sorted.

Pilot packages (indicative):
- Pilot Lite (90 days): 1 GPU worker, 2 CPU workers, basic monitoring — good for PoC — ~£12k fixed + usage.
- Pilot Standard (90 days): 2 GPU workers, 3 CPU workers, 30-day retention logs + onboarding support — ~£28k fixed + usage.
- Pilot Enterprise (90 days): Dedicated control plane, HSM integration support, extended SLAs, and 3rd-party audit support — pricing on request.

We’ll attach a pricing matrix (pricing-matrix-v2.csv) with line items and what’s included. Key commercial note: HSM integration and on-site support are often scoped as an enterprise add-on. If Cinderford needs an on-prem engineer for the cutover week, we can include a 5-day coverage line.

A couple of deployment constraints from ops that impact pricing:
- If you require host-level disk encryption with customer-owned keys (HSM unseal on boot), we need a stretch window to validate the unseal workflow — that’s an extra 1–2 days of validation.
- Network egress constraints that block outbound to our control plane will move you to a fully air-gapped deployment, which increases the effort.

Helen — are you expecting SOW-level commitment this month or next? Vivek, FYI on potential timeline and ACV.

Thanks,

Thanks Helen — that latency profile looks fine for the suggested unseal/bootstrap workflow. Short answers to your KMS questions:

- Yes: we can support a model where the HSM generates wrapping keys and never exports the raw key material. Our agent uses KMIP to request wrap/unwrap operations; the unwrapped data key is held in-memory on the node and discarded on pod termination. For disk-level encryption (dm-crypt/LUKS), we can use an HSM-wrapped key that the node unseals via KMIP at boot.
- For model artifact encryption: recommended pattern is to have a site-local envelope key generated by your HSM; model artifacts are encrypted with ephemeral data keys that are wrapped by the envelope key. That way keys never leave the HSM in plaintext.
